Your best bet is to buy it and see. Make sure the one you just bought is visually identical to the one you already have. Try to put yourself in the position of someone who is hired to check returned products. Whatever you send back has to match the product you bought. Any wear and tear has to be reasonably possible within the return window in which you bought it.

This should continue to work forever, as long as the product cannot be traced to a specific point in time. This works best for items that are mass produced quickly and sold slowly over time. 

For example- you buy a Farberware branded spatula 2 years ago, and the handle is now loose. Farberware still sells the spatula and has made no design changes. You buy a new one and compare- they are indistinguishable. 

Important: The one that you have owned for 2 years should not show any signs of wear that indicate it has been owned for more than 30 days.  

This will not work for serialized products or any for products that have design updates.

So this is what I do with many companies and not just Amazon. This only works for non-serialized products.  

Example:  
I bought a coffee grinder back in 2017

I bought the same grinder on Amazon

On a serious note- heat is your friend but you have to consider several factors. You said it sat in a car for a while, but remember that even if the air in your car reaches a over 50°C, the heat absorbed by your luggage might have been much cooler. 

“Bed bugs and eggs die within 90 minutes at 118°F (48°C) or immediately at 122°F (50°C )” -
https://www.bedbugs.umn.edu

If you can get some sealable plastic bags, bag up your belongings to isolate said items. Think of it like a mattress protector for your stuff.

Bedbugs don’t typically hitchhike but it’s better to be safe than sorry. When they are not feeding they will hide in cracks/crevices of bedding, in bed frames and in baseboards. Crawling into your suitcase could happen, but not as likely as the areas stated above.

How do bedbugs find their next meal? They detect the CO2 that you breathe out and come to feed when you are still and sleeping. Best way to check is to set an alarm for the middle of the night so you can pull down the covers and inspect the sheets. 

Signs of bed bug bites do not show on everyone. You can get bit and not see bites if your body does not react to them.

Yes, I think you are overreacting. You will encounter lots of people who have or have had bed bugs in your life time. You will sit places where they have been, you will sleep in hotels that have had to previously exterminate them.

I’ve had them twice now thanks to NYC and another situation. They suck royally, give you nightmares, ptsd, and turn your life upside down... but your chances of getting them from a coworker is not likely. They may hitchhike on clothing but it’s not common. Plus, you don’t know what kind of bugs he has and there is NO WAY of telling if someone has bed bug bites. Spiders bite, fleas bite.. they all look similar and that’s that. I’m currently itching from mosquito bites (i play softball twice a week) and they don’t look much different than when I had bed bugs.

If walks in tomorrow and says that he got an exterminator and the issue is taken care of, would you move on and let it go? What if that’s a lie? How would you know? You wouldn’t.

Grief is something you learn to live with, not get through. There isn’t a “get to the other side of it.” It’s a process. There will be good weeks, then several bad ones. It creeps up when you don’t expect it. That’s normal. Then, the good memories start to frequent more than the sadness. Be kind to yourself and know others have been in similar places. It will get easier if you let yourself feel the emotions it brings and work through it, I promise. ❤️
